children: The Dighi project is expected to create 15,000 direct and 75,000 indirect jobs while expanding India’s shipbuilding capacity

Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders (MDL) will invest around Rs 27,000 crore to establish a greenfield shipbuilding cluster at Dighi in Maharashtra’s Raigad district, with the project expected to generate around 90,000 jobs.

MDL has signed a memorandum of understanding with National Shipbuilding and Heavy Industries Park Maharashtra Ltd for the project. The proposed facility is expected to create around 15,000 direct jobs and 75,000 indirect employment opportunities, according to the Maharashtra government.

The cluster will target an annual shipbuilding capacity of at least 2 million gross tonnes and is planned to support the construction of large commercial vessels. The project will also create an industrial and supply chain ecosystem around shipbuilding, opening employment opportunities across manufacturing, engineering, logistics, marine services and related industries.

The proposed shipyard is expected to include shipbuilding, repair, recycling and other maritime activities. The project is being developed under the Centre’s Greenfield Shipbuilding Cluster Development Plan and is aligned with the Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047.

Work on the project is expected to begin after the required approvals, with the Maharashtra government indicating a completion timeline of around three years. The employment impact will depend on the project’s implementation and the development of its wider industrial ecosystem.
